describe.chat: Stage a find-and-replace across the draft: every match in headings, eyebrows, body, quotes, alt text, spoken lines, notes and descriptions. It works the way a word processor does: the words change and their formatting stays (replace `Oct` in **Oct** and it stays bold). Write the replacement as plain words; characters Markdown would read as markup (`$`, `*`, `[`…) are escaped for you, so `$5` shows as $5. It never touches link or image targets, URLs, directives, code blocks, math, HTML, `{…}` records or the front matter; a match that crosses formatting (`**Oct.** Tenth`) is left alone; it reports what it left alone (for terms in the front matter use set_terms). Literal text, not a pattern; with case_sensitive false the replacement is written exactly as given. For a word or phrase change use this, not edit_slides: you send only the words, and the author reviews one card. The result includes the checker’s verdict on the draft.

find.description: The words to replace, up to {{FIND_MAX_CHARS}} characters.

replace.description: What to write instead. One line; may be empty to delete the words.

whole_word.description: Match whole words only. Default false.

slides.description: Only these slides. Default: every slide.

summary.description: One or two sentences to the author: what you changed and why. If the checker finds no errors this is your whole answer for the turn.
